```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(knbsdata)
```

This vignette covers finding a survey, reading its documentation and
understanding what you are and are not allowed to do with it.

Every code chunk that contacts the archive is shown but not run, so that
building this vignette never depends on a live service.

## What is supported

`knbs_sources()` reports what the package knows about each source and how far it
has been verified. Nothing here makes a request:

```{r}
knbs_sources(operation = "search_surveys")
```

The survey catalogue is the Kenya National Data Archive, which exposes a JSON
API. It is registered as `experimental`: the endpoints are verified and covered
by tests, but the archive does not document the API, so it could change without
notice. If it does, the package raises a `knbs_error_schema_changed` rather than
returning something plausible.

## Finding a survey

```{r, eval = FALSE}
studies <- knbs_search_surveys("household budget")
studies
```

You can filter by reference year, by producer and by access type:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_search_surveys(year = c(2015, 2020))
knbs_search_surveys(access = "public_use", limit = 10)
```

Three columns come back as `NA` from a search: `acronym`,
`geographic_coverage` and `unit_of_analysis`. They live in the study record
rather than the catalogue index, and filling them in would mean one extra
request per row. `knbs_survey_metadata()` retrieves them.

## Reading a study's documentation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
meta <- knbs_survey_metadata("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01")
meta
```

The printed record shows the title, reference period, producer, geographic
coverage, unit of analysis and access type. The full descriptive sections are in
`meta$sections`; `include` narrows them:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_survey_metadata("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01", include = c("scope", "access"))
```

These records are DDI documents, in which sampling, data collection and
processing all live in a single `method` section, so asking for any one of those
returns that section.

You do not have to know the exact identifier. Give it something recognisable and
it will search the catalogue; if more than one study matches you get an error
listing the candidates rather than a silently chosen "best" match.

## Searching variables

Variable metadata are available without downloading any microdata:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_variables("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01", search = "expenditure")
knbs_variables("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01", file = "HH_Information")
```

`search` matches variable names and labels, and matches nothing else. If a
concept you expect is missing, it is worth listing all the variables and looking
at the labels the study actually uses before concluding the search is broken.

Question text, universe, concept and value labels each cost one request per
variable, so they are empty unless you ask:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_variables(
  "KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01",
  search = "county",
  details = TRUE
)
```

That is capped at 100 variables. Narrow the selection first rather than raising
the cap.

Some studies are catalogued with no variable documentation at all — including,
at the time of writing, the most recent one. That returns zero rows, which is an
answer rather than a failure.

## Files, and what you may do with them

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_survey_files("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01")
```

Two columns matter most:

- `access_type` describes the archive's terms. `public_use` means public-use
  files exist. It does **not** mean they can be downloaded without an account.
- `downloadable` describes what this package will do. At present it is `FALSE`
  for every file from every supported source.

## Downloading microdata

You cannot do this through `knbsdata`, and that is deliberate:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_download_microdata("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01")
#> Error: Microdata from "kenada" cannot be downloaded programmatically.
#> x Every download requires an account with the archive.
#> i Register and request access at <https://statistics.knbs.or.ke/nada/index.php/home>.
#> i knbsdata does not automate sign-in, licence acceptance or approval workflows.
```

The archive puts every download behind a login. The package does not automate
sign-in, licence acceptance or approval workflows, so the function exists purely
to fail clearly and point you at the official process. Complete that process,
download the files yourself, and read them with `readr`, `haven` or whatever
suits the format.

This matters for a subtler reason too. The gate is signalled by an HTTP
`Refresh` header rather than a redirect status, so a client that only checks the
status code sees `200 OK` and an empty body — and could report "no data" where
the honest answer is "you need an account". The package treats that as an
authentication error.

## Citing what you used

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_cite(meta)
```

Where the archive states a required citation, that text is used and the package
adds the retrieval date and its own version. `knbs_metadata()` shows the full
provenance record behind any object.

## Caching

Catalogue responses are cached for 24 hours by default:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_cache_info()
knbs_search_surveys("household budget", refresh = TRUE)  # bypass the cache
knbs_cache_clear()
```

Cache entries are checksummed and keyed partly on the package's parser version,
so upgrading the package invalidates anything a new parser would read
differently.
